system_description.narrative_title: Energy shocks, inflation, and tech as strategic power in a fractured order
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system where renewed Middle East violence (Iran, Houthis) is disrupting oil and shipping chokepoints, feeding an inflation shock that ripples through bond markets and fiscal space. At the same time strategic competition over advanced technology and AI is re‑casting infrastructure and intelligence vulnerabilities, while states hedge through new alignments (BRICS, China‑India outreach) and regional balancing. These interacting processes — energy security, financial instability, and techno‑strategic rivalry — are driving short‑term volatility and long‑term realignments in capabilities, supply chains and alliances.
system_description.scope: Interstate politics and conflicts, global energy and maritime security (oil, chokepoints), international financial and sovereign bond markets, central bank and fiscal responses, strategic technology/AI infrastructure and governance, major-power diplomacy and bloc formation (BRICS, NATO, GCC), and supply‑chain/commodity flows that mediate domestic economic outcomes.
system_description.super_system: The global political‑economic system (world order embedded in the planetary economy, ecology and transnational governance frameworks).
adjacent_subsystems: Global Energy and Maritime Security (oil flows, chokepoints, tankers)
International Financial Markets & Monetary Policy (bonds, rates, inflation)
Global Technology & AI Governance (data centers, AI models, dual‑use tech)
Regional Security Architectures and Multilateral Blocs (BRICS, GCC, NATO)

variables.name: Iran-led regional escalation
variables.description: Iran, the United States, Gulf states and Iran-aligned proxies are locked in a widening confrontation as Tehran tests limits of escalation and regional security balances shift.

variables.name: Energy supply and maritime chokepoints
variables.description: Attacks and disruptions by regional actors and proxies involving Gulf producers and transit-route users are compressing oil and refined-fuel flows and driving volatile global energy prices.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and European burden
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain in protracted high-intensity conflict while NATO partners and European states face rising military, political and financial strains as the war grinds on.

variables.name: Global bond and rate shock
variables.description: Coordinated shifts in monetary policy from the US Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and other major central banks are producing a sustained rise in sovereign yields that is reordering capital flows and fiscal pressures worldwide.

variables.name: US–China technology and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting dominance in semiconductors, AI and high-tech supply chains while other powers, including India and BRICS members, hedge, realign economic ties and build alternative financial links.
